{{Quote|Going somewhere, Solo?|Greedo, to Han Solo|translated=1|audio=Greedo-ANH.flac|<ref name="Sounds">''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]''</ref>}}
'''Greedo''', son of [[Greedo the Elder]], was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]. He lived in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] alongside the young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[W. Wald]] circa [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Although his father had been an esteemed hunter, and the chief rival of [[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red]], the younger Greedo had little of his father's prowess and was easily killed by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
[[File:Young_Greedo.jpg|thumb|left|Young Greedo]]
{{Quote|Why did you never tell Pqweeduk and me about the ships&#32;... and about our people?|Greedo, following a discussion with his mother, Neela, about their violent past|<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" />}}
Greedo was born on [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] within the ranks of the persecuted [[Tetsu Clan]]. His father, [[Greedo the Elder]], was a well-known [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] whose successes made his family very wealthy. A rival, [[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red]], leader of the powerful [[Chattza clan/Legends|Chattza Clan]], targeted the Tetsus, brutally murdering the elder Greedo and taking their wealth. His pregnant wife, [[Neela]], took her son and father's namesake, along with other Tetsu Rodians, and fled the planet. Settling on a remote jungle planet<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/webstrips/greedo/index.html?show=1|text=A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale|int=A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale (webstrip)}}</ref> [[U-Tendik]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> the refugees began to rebuild their lives. A pact was made between the clan elders to never tell the children of their violent past.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

Greedo and his younger brother [[Pqweeduk]] spent over ten years on that planet. It was the only life he knew; the tall [[Tendril tree]]s, the water, and the endless days of play. The clan elders were careful to keep details of their past hidden, though Greedo often overheard such discussions. The terminology used was unfamiliar to him, as the isolation of refugee life did not expose him to otherwise commonplace things such as the [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and bounty hunters. His imagination would have continued to run wild until the day when he discovered clues to another life beyond the jungle.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

As a teenager, Greedo led his brother Pqweeduk deep into the jungle, away from their small village and to a hidden cavern. Within the cavern were three large silver ships, sitting silently in the darkness. A sense of familiarity was stirred, though Greedo could not attach a memory to it. However, it was enough for him to want to know more. That night after his brother had gone to sleep, Greedo asked his mother about the hidden ships.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

Neela was hesitant at first to divulge such information, lamenting that "[[Nok (Rodian)|Nok]] loves the past too much," but she gave in, seeing that her son was not about to let his discovery go. Greedo was told only the details his mother felt were relevant to that discussion, including the [[Rodian Clan Wars]] and the murder of his father.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

[[File:GreedoTheElderTPM.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Greedo on Tatooine in his youth]]
A month and a day passed when the Tetsu Clan was finally tracked down by Navik the Red. In a flurry of activity, Navik's Chattza warriors descended on the hapless population, killing a number and dispersing the rest. Greedo, Pqweeduk, and Neela barely escaped the carnage and fled into the dense jungle, regrouping with Neela's brothers, Nok and [[Teeku]]. Nok explained why he had been visiting the ships, as he was maintaining them in preparation in the event that the clan would need to be evacuated. That day had arrived. The panic-stricken Tetsu Rodians hurried to board the three ships as their pursuers tracked them through the jungle. One of the ships was destroyed before it could close its hatch.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

Greedo's family and the surviving twenty Tetsus that came with them, however, escaped in the ''[[Radion]]'', making the pre-programmed jump to [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], where they hoped to be lost among the myriad of [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] traffic that flocked around the heavily-populated [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. There Greedo was exposed to the commonplace aspects of the galaxy, learning the ins and outs of the [[Black market/Legends|black market]], thanks to the teachings of his friend [[Anky Fremp]], a [[Skup/Legends|Skup]] biomorph. They had been a team for years, stripping [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] floaters of parts and selling the hardware to the highest bidder. Greedo's social development had grown, becoming familiar with the things that used to be foreign to him.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

===Moving to Tatooine===
[[File:PapanoidaIonNabbed_SoI.png|thumb|left|250px|Greedo and friends subdue Notluwiski Papanoida and Ion Papanoida.]]
Eventually, the family ended up moving to Tatooine,<ref name="Not-So Magnificient Seven" /> During Greedo's time on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Greedo was noted for his temper. He accused young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] of cheating in the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]], resulting in a scuffle that [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] had to break up. His friend [[W. Wald]] warned him that if he continued his violent ways, he would eventually come to a bad end.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}} {{C|[[Content cut from Star Wars#Episode I The Phantom Menace|deleted scene]]}}</ref><ref name="SWEGreedo">{{SWE|characters|greedo|Greedo}}</ref> Greedo eventually became a thug and turned to petty crime, spending much of the time in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] handging and playing games of chance with other big name wannabees.<ref name="Not-So Magnificient Seven" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Greedo still resided on Tatooine. At some time during the war, he traveled to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and kidnapped [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Notluwiski Papanoida/Legends|Notluwiski Papanoida's]] daughters, [[Che Amanwe Papanoida/Legends|Che Amanwe]] and [[Chi Eekway Papanoida/Legends|Chi Eekway]], with the help of another [[Unidentified Gotal bounty hunter/Legends|mercenary]]. The chairman of [[Pantora/Legends|Pantora]] and his son [[Ion Papanoida/Legends|Ion]] tracked the Rodian bounty hunter to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] and forced him to help them retrieve Che Amanwe from [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. When they arrived at the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|cantina]] where Che Amanwe was held, Greedo turned on the [[Pantoran/Legends|Pantorans]], causing the patrons at the cantina to fire upon them while the Rodian slipped out of the area.<ref name="Sphere of Influence" />

===Imperial Period===
[[File:Swk_greedo.jpg|thumb|250px|Greedo in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]].]]
At some point after the end of the Clone Wars, Greedo moved back to Nar Shaddaa. He still retained a level of naivete, all too eager to sell out the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] to the Empire in order to make a quick profit. Life on Nar Shaddaa fueled Greedo's fascination with bounty hunters. He idolized them and wished to become one. Greedo saved the lives of two bounty hunters, [[Spurch Goa|Spurch "Warhog" Goa]] and his partner [[Dyyz Nataz]], when they were attacked by the cyborg [[Gorm (cyborg)|Gorm]], becoming the only being ever known to have actually hit the towering droid. In return, the pair of hunters cut Greedo in on a bounty for killing a rogue Imperial spice inspector. As a thank-you, Greedo told them about a Rebel enclave in Level 88. With the Imperial reward Greedo intended to buy his own ship, [[Manka Hunter|''The Manka Hunter'']], but was tricked out of most of his share by Warhog. Greedo tried to lessen the price by stealing some [[Power coupling/Legends|power couplings]] from another ship. Unfortunately, those couplings were for the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], and an angry [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] caught him in the act. As restitution, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] took Greedo's [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]]-skin jacket in exchange for the pair of burnt-out couplings just taken off the ''Falcon''. Greedo threatened revenge. Goa taught Greedo to be a bounty hunter and Greedo thought he would become a great one, learning from a "master." Soon enough, though, he started to regret his decision when the Imperials attacked the Rebels in Level 88. Greedo, Dyyz, and Goa escaped in Goa's ship, the ''[[Nova Viper]]'', just as Level 88 caught fire,<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" /> killing Greedo's whole family.<ref name="NEGC" />

===The Yavin Vassilika and death===
{{Quote|That's the idea. I've been looking forward to this for a long time.|translated=1|Greedo's last words|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:Greedo-SWIANH.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Greedo's last moments before being shot by Han Solo]]
Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Greedo rented a small ship and tagged along on the hunt for the [[Yavin Vassilika]]. He hob-nobbed with the galaxy's greatest hunters, though he himself was profoundly out of his element. Nevertheless, he had gotten a taste of the trade.<ref name="Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> Upon his return to Tatooine, Greedo continued working with [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]], securing a contract on Han Solo, with Goa also being involved in the contract. Greedo had encountered Solo twice, demanding payment, but was humiliated both times.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" /> He eventually met up with Solo again in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] where Greedo demanded Jabba's cut. Solo, not having that amount of money just yet, was forced to find another solution. Solo prepared his blaster under the table they were sitting at and shot the inexperienced bounty hunter from below. Greedo himself had managed to pull off a shot less than a second before, but missed entirely. Solo then stood up, threw a coin to the bartender, apologizing for the mess, and left the cantina for [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]].<ref name="ANH" /> Although Greedo's death was on Solo's hands, it was actually Greedo's "mentor," Warhog Goa who should be credited with his demise. Goa had tricked an over-matched Greedo into going against Solo after receiving a payoff from two Rodian bounty hunters who were tracking the young novice. Goa, alongside the Rodian bounty hunters, also bore witness to Greedo's death.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate webstrip" />

After Greedo's death, [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] and his new droid companion, [[C2-R4]], claimed the bounty hunter's body and ground it up into a powerful [[Liqueur/Legends|liqueur]]. All that remained of Greedo afterward was his head, which Wuher (having taken a dislike to Greedo while he was still alive) impaled on a spike.<ref name="BSMH TBT">{{StoryCite|story=Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Greedo was as delusional as Bossk.|[[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], in response to the late Greedo's anecdotes on ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]''|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
[[File:GreedoFuneral.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Bounty hunters attend the [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] for Greedo]]
Greedo's social ineptitude led many, including his uncle [[Avaro Sookcool]], to perceive him as "not very bright."<ref name="We Don't Do Weddings">{{StoryCite|story=We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref><ref name="SotE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref> By the time of the Clone Wars he had gotten a feel for what being a bounty hunter would be like and modeled his reactions as such. This change was even more evident when Greedo pursued the bounty on Dionisio. He knew where to go for information and how to complete a mission, giving him a boost of confidence for when he took the contract on Solo.<ref name="Hovel">{{Tales|6|The Hovel on Terk Street}}</ref> His excitability was reduced and his complaining was almost non-existent. However, Greedo was still making amateur mistakes, such as allowing Nok Derrick to get the drop on him in a dark alley.<ref name="Hovel" /> Some maintained that he was not entirely vigilant to his surroundings, nervous, easily spooked, over-confident and he often complained.<ref name="Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate story" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal===
[[File:GreedoUnmasked.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Maria De Aragon on the set as Greedo.]]
[[Paul Blake]] played Greedo in the shots that feature both Greedo and Han Solo in the same frame. For Greedo's close-ups, a new articulated head was built for pickups at the end of the shoot, and [[Maria De Aragon]] was enlisted to play the Rodian. Greedo's language was actually [[Wikipedia:Quechua|Quechua]], a native language of [[Wikipedia:South America|South America]]. During pickups, Greedo's costume vest changes significantly, as do his hands. In the original shoot, Greedo has long, suction-cup tipped fingers, and in pickups, he has swollen knuckles and shorter fingers. In ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' TV series he was voiced by [[Tom Kenny]].

===Continuity===
Both Greedo's backstory and the circumstances of his death have been subject to a number of [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]]s over the years. The most famous involves the question of [[Han shot first|who shot first]], for in the original [[1977]] release of the film, as well as the script, Greedo did not shoot at Han at all. In the [[List of changes in Star Wars re-releases#1997 special editions|1997 re-release of the film]], Greedo gets a badly-aimed shot at Solo before Solo kills him. [[George Lucas]] has said that this change is to enhance Solo's overall heroism, and to not portray him as a cold-blooded killer. This was a controversial decision and in the 2004 version the two shots are almost simultaneous, with Greedo shooting first.

The short story ''[[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale]]'' presents Greedo's famous line as "Oona goota, Solo?" whereas the [[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']] and the ''[[Star Wars PocketModel TCG]]'' establish the spelling as "Koona t'chuta, Solo?". The latter sources are more current. Throughout ''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'', it is implied that Greedo's spoken language is [[Rodese/Legends|Rodese]], not Huttese, and he does not even seem to understand the language of the Hutts. This is contradicted by later official sources that verify Greedo is speaking Huttese.

[[File:Greedos_demise.png|thumb|right|250px|The canonical death of Greedo]]
Greedo's backstory was established in ''[[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale]]'' short story, published in the ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'' in [[1995]] and later adapted into a webstrip of the same name. In a deleted scene from [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], included on the [[2001]] [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD release]], a character named Greedo appears fighting in the street with a young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. After the fight is broken up by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], Greedo is warned by fellow Rodian [[W. Wald]] that some day his actions will result in him coming to "a bad end". Despite George Lucas' insistence that this was the same Greedo from ''A New Hope'', the scene was felt to be in conflict with established [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] history and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the Rodian who fought with Anakin to be [[Greedo the Elder]]&mdash;Greedo's father. However, in 2010 the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode ''[[Sphere of Influence]]'' featured Greedo as an adult on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and firmly established him to be same character as seen in both Episode IV and Episode I.<ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=message.jspa?messageID=17933823#17933823|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2010-10-04|time=10:33 AM}}</ref> For some time the canonicity of ''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'' remained unclear, for example the description of its events was removed from Greedo's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry. In [[2013]] however, a [[StarWars.com]] blog article ''[[The Not-So Magnificent Seven]]'' explicitly referenced those events, tying them up with Greedo's appearance in ''The Clone Wars'', reestablishing its canonical status. Despite that, the dating of events given in ''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'' contradicts the current canonical version. According to the short story, Greedo was only born around [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]] and all of his childhood was spend during the reign of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Any references to those events by dating remain incompatible with the current version of Greedo being a child by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and an adolescent by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

The Rodian thugs seen in ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' were based on Greedo. All of them are alike and are dressed the same way as Greedo. Also, on the back of the box, it calls all Rodians "Greedo." In the sequel to the above game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'', all the Rodians are also dressed similarly to Greedo; though a few are slightly different in what they wear. As a nod to the original character, the multiplayer gives the Rodian's BOT name as 'Beedo'.

Greedo's height has varied between various sources. His height is 1.65 meters in ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'', ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'', whereas the Rodian's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry gives a height of 1.8 meters. To add to further confusion, Greedo's ''[[Clone Cards]]'' entry says that he is 1.74 meters tall, and his data in ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'' provides a height of 1.73 meters. This article uses the latter source as it is the most current.
